4	/// The recorder panel's window picker (road map 3, R1c) —
5	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s fifth file, cut out of `+Recording.swift`
6	/// along the line `presentPicker` draws when the R1 review's fixes put that
7	/// file past the 400-line cap. The Source row's last item, "Window…",
8	/// presents `SCContentSharingPicker` in single-window mode; the filter it
9	/// answers with is held in `pickedFilter` beside the choice (a filter is not
10	/// a value, so `.picked` is the one source that cannot persist), and a
11	/// cancel or a failure puts the Source row back on the display the person
12	/// last chose. Record with the row reading "Window…" and no filter held is
13	/// refused by name in `+Recording.swift`, never answered by presenting the
14	/// picker from the guard.
15	extension RecorderPanelController {
16	    // MARK: - The window picker
17	
18	    /// `SCContentSharingPicker` in single-window mode, what
19	    /// `recordingExclusion(includeFrameJobWindows:)` names excluded from the
20	    /// LIST — Frame Job's application with Include Frame Job windows off, the
21	    /// panel's own window alone with it on (spec §11 recording.md).
22	    /// `excludedBundleIDs` is documented "for picking" and says nothing about
23	    /// capture (R0 q3), which is why R1 hid the panel for a picked window
24	    /// alone; since R2 every recording hides it (decision 7), and the
25	    /// exclusion is about the list only. The observer is added once; the
26	    /// picker is activated for the presentation and deactivated when it
27	    /// answers.
28	    func presentPicker() {
29	        let exclusion = recordingExclusion(
30	            includeFrameJobWindows: includeFrameJobCheckbox.state == .on)
31	        let picker = SCContentSharingPicker.shared
32	        if !pickerObserved {
33	            picker.add(self)
34	            pickerObserved = true
35	        }
36	        var configuration = SCContentSharingPickerConfiguration()
37	        configuration.allowedPickerModes = [.singleWindow]
38	        configuration.excludedBundleIDs = exclusion.bundleIDs
39	        configuration.excludedWindowIDs = exclusion.windowIDs.map { Int($0) }
40	        picker.defaultConfiguration = configuration
41	        picker.isActive = true
42	        picker.present(using: .window)
43	    }
44	
45	    /// What a display recording and the picker leave out (spec §11
46	    /// recording.md, Include Frame Job windows): Frame Job's application with
47	    /// the box off; with it on, the panel's own window, which is on screen
48	    /// until `recordingDidStart` — after the file's first frame (R0 q2).
49	    func recordingExclusion(includeFrameJobWindows: Bool) -> RecordingExclusion {
50	        let number = window?.windowNumber ?? 0
51	        return RecordingExclusion.make(
52	            includeFrameJobWindows: includeFrameJobWindows,
53	            ownBundleID: Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier,
54	            panelWindowID: number > 0 ? CGWindowID(clamping: number) : nil)
55	    }
56	
57	    /// Back to the display the person last chose (the persisted one), with
58	    /// the Window row reading "Window…" again.
59	    private func revertSourceRow() {
60	        pickedFilter = nil
61	        sourcePopup.menu?.item(withTag: Self.windowTag)?.title = "Window…"
62	        let stored = UserDefaults.standard.integer(forKey: Self.displayKey)
63	        selectDisplay(stored > 0 ? CGDirectDisplayID(clamping: stored) : CGMainDisplayID())
64	        refreshSizeNote()
65	    }
66	}

13	/// display key is left alone while it is chosen. Chosen, it greys System

40	/// precedent, `hidesForRecording`): nothing on screen is filmed, so the rows
41	/// lock, the meter is live, and Record reads Stop with the Pause / Resume
42	/// button beside it.

49	/// the Window row, and greyed with its value kept under Camera or Microphone
50	/// Only. Ticked, a camera is WANTED as with Source Camera: the Camera and
51	/// Format popups are live, the choice carries `camera` and `cameraFormat`
52	/// beside the screen source, and the preview shows. The five screen controls
53	/// stay live, and the press (`+Recording.swift`) reads Screen Recording, then
54	/// Camera, then Microphone.
55	extension RecorderPanelController {
56	    static let cameraTag = 3
57	    static let cameraTitle = "Camera"
58	    static let noCameraTitle = "None connected"
59	    static let bestFormatTitle = "Best"
60	
61	    var cameraSelected: Bool { sourcePopup.selectedItem?.tag == Self.cameraTag }
62	
63	    /// A display row or the Window row: the sources the box is live for.

4	/// What the camera preview's well does at one sync (spec §11 CAM-7 (3)).
5	enum CameraPreviewStep: Equatable {
6	    case off
7	    case message(String)
8	    case failed(String)
9	    case prepare
10	    case prepared
11	    case recording
12	    case blank
13	}
14	
15	/// The camera's live preview in the panel (camera-recording CR2b, spec §11
16	/// CAM-7) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s eleventh file, NEW rather than
17	/// cut, as `+Camera.swift` was: the rule that says what the well shows, and
18	/// the one sync that acts on it. The well is `CameraPreviewWell`, a grid row
19	/// of its own right under Format (`+Rows.swift`), shown only while a camera
20	/// is wanted: Source Camera, or "Record the camera too" beside a screen
21	/// source (spec §11 CAM-11 (4)).
22	///
23	/// **The step** (`cameraPreviewStep`, pure, first match wins): a panel not
24	/// visible or closing, or no camera wanted → off; a camera recording, or a
25	/// screen recording's camera beside it → its layer; the countdown or
26	/// starting → the prepared layer, never a build; any other phase, or a
27	/// busy recorder → blank; no camera → "No camera is connected."; the
28	/// Camera grant not authorized → a sentence; a prepared capture that
29	/// failed, or a build that threw → its sentence, never retried; else
30	/// prepare. The grant is read only at its own step, through
31	/// `grantDoors.cameraStatus`, so showing the panel never prompts and a
32	/// hidden panel reads nothing.
33	///
34	/// **The sync** runs at the end of `show()`, of every control change, of
35	/// `syncPhase()`, at the one-second tick while the panel is visible, and at
36	/// each device notification. Its first act applies a pending hot-plug
37	/// (`+Devices.swift`, CAM-8 (2)), so the step sees the new selection. It
38	/// keeps the row's visibility (refitting the window when it changes), lets
39	/// the prepared capture go when the well is off or shows a sentence while
40	/// everything is idle, stops a failed prepared capture once (not at every
41	/// tick, CAM-8 (6)), and otherwise hosts the layer the step names. The
42	/// capture is the recorder's (`ScreenRecorder+CameraPrepare.swift`): the
43	/// countdown's `prepareCamera` keeps it, the panel's start adopts it, and a
44	/// tool's start never does (CAM-7 (7)), so through a tool's recording the
45	/// well reads "The camera is recording."
46	extension RecorderPanelController {
47	    static let previewGrantSentence = "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera."
48	    static let previewRecordingSentence = "The camera is recording."
49	
50	    /// CAM-7 (3)'s rule. `grant` and `failure` are called only at their own
51	    /// steps.
52	    static func cameraPreviewStep(
53	        visible: Bool, cameraSource: Bool, phase: Phase, recorderIdle: Bool,
54	        recordingCamera: Bool, cameraChosen: Bool, grant: () -> AVAuthorizationStatus,
55	        failure: () -> String?
56	    ) -> CameraPreviewStep {
57	        guard visible, cameraSource else { return .off }
58	        if recordingCamera { return .recording }
59	        switch phase {
60	        case .countdown, .starting: return .prepared
61	        case .idle: break
62	        case .recording, .paused, .stopping, .landing: return .blank
63	        }
64	        guard recorderIdle else { return .blank }
65	        guard cameraChosen else { return .message(CameraDevices.noCameraSentence) }
66	        guard grant() == .authorized else { return .message(Self.previewGrantSentence) }
67	        if let failure = failure() { return .failed(failure) }
68	        return .prepare
69	    }
70	
71	    /// The well's grid row.
72	    var cameraPreviewRow: NSGridRow? {
73	        (cameraPreview.superview as? NSGridView)?.cell(for: cameraPreview)?.row
74	    }
75	
76	    /// For the chosen camera at its resolved format (CAM-6 (3)): the
77	    /// prepared capture's stop on its own, else its failed start, else a
78	    /// failed build's record; nil when there is none.
79	    var previewFailure: String? {
80	        guard let id = selectedCameraID, let device = CameraDevices.device(withID: id) else {
81	            return nil
82	        }
83	        let facts = CameraDevices.facts(of: device)
84	        guard
85	            let format = CameraDevices.chosenFormat(
86	                selectedCameraFormat, in: facts.formats, active: facts.activeFormat)
87	        else { return nil }
88	        if let prepared = recorder.preparedCamera, prepared.deviceID == id, prepared.format == format,
89	            let sentence = prepared.stoppedOnItsOwn ?? prepared.startError?.localizedDescription
90	        {
91	            return sentence
92	        }
93	        guard let failure = recorder.preparedCameraFailure, failure.deviceID == id,
94	            failure.format == format
95	        else { return nil }
96	        return failure.sentence
97	    }
98	
99	    /// A pending hot-plug applied (CAM-8 (2)), the row's visibility, then the
100	    /// step acted on (the type doc).
101	    func syncCameraPreview() {
102	        applyPendingDevices()
103	        let hidden = !cameraWanted
104	        if let row = cameraPreviewRow, row.isHidden != hidden {
105	            row.isHidden = hidden
106	            fitWindowToContent()
107	        }
108	        let step = Self.cameraPreviewStep(
109	            visible: window?.isVisible == true && !panelClosing, cameraSource: cameraWanted,
110	            phase: phase, recorderIdle: recorder.state == .idle,
111	            recordingCamera: recorder.cameraSession != nil || recorder.session?.cameraCapture != nil,
112	            cameraChosen: selectedCameraID != nil,
113	            grant: { Self.grantDoors.cameraStatus() }, failure: { self.previewFailure })
114	        switch step {
115	        case .off, .message:
116	            if phase == .idle, recorder.state == .idle { recorder.discardPreparedCamera() }
117	            if case .message(let sentence) = step {
118	                cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
119	            } else {
120	                cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
121	            }
122	        case .failed(let sentence):
123	            if let capture = recorder.preparedCamera?.capture, !capture.stopped { capture.stop() }
124	            cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
125	        case .prepare:
126	            recorder.prepareCamera(for: currentChoice())
127	            hostPreview(recorder.preparedCamera?.capture.previewLayer, else: nil)
128	        case .prepared:
129	            hostPreview(recorder.preparedCamera?.capture.previewLayer, else: nil)
130	        case .recording:
131	            hostPreview(
132	                (recorder.cameraSession?.capture ?? recorder.session?.cameraCapture)?.previewLayer,
133	                else: Self.previewRecordingSentence)
134	        case .blank:
135	            cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
136	        }
137	    }
138	
139	    /// `layer` in the well, else `sentence` (nil a blank well).
140	    private func hostPreview(_ layer: AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer?, else sentence: String?) {
141	        if let layer {
142	            cameraPreview.show(layer)
143	        } else {
144	            cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
145	        }
146	    }
147	}

3	/// Pause and resume from the panel's side, the one door into a hidden
4	/// recording's controls, and the phases drawn (road map 3, R2c) —
5	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s sixth file, NEW rather than cut for its
6	/// first two members: they are the whole of what the panel adds for a pause,
7	/// and `+Recording.swift` and the base file were both within a dozen lines
8	/// of the 400-line cap when R2 began. `syncPhase` and `refreshStatusLabel`
9	/// then MOVED here from the base file when the R2 review's fixes took it
10	/// over the cap — the base file's toll, paid along the line the footnote
11	/// draws: its `.paused` and `.stopping` arms are what the pause added, and
12	/// `syncPhase` is its one caller besides the tick.
13	///
14	/// **Neither pause member is reachable from the panel's own controls** but
15	/// in a voice-over, whose panel stays up with a Pause / Resume button
16	/// (`+VoiceOver.swift`). The panel is off screen for every other recording
17	/// (decision 7), so Pause Recording
18	/// and Resume Recording are rows of the status item's menu, which calls
19	/// these through the closures `recordingDidStart` hands it, and File ▸
20	/// Pause/Resume Recording (`AppDelegate+Recording.swift`), the second door,
21	/// which calls them for the panel's own recording (#98). The panel's
22	/// phase — `.recording ⇄ .paused` — follows the recorder's own `pause()` /
23	/// `resume()` (`ScreenRecorder+Pause.swift`), which are synchronous and
24	/// throw. The phase moves only AFTER the call returns
25	/// without throwing, so the panel never claims a state the recorder
26	/// refused: a pause that could not close the segment's file leaves the
27	/// recorder `.recording` and the panel with it, and a resume whose output
28	/// could not be added leaves both `.paused`.
29	///
30	/// **The two refusals are answered differently, on purpose.** A refused
31	/// pause BEEPS: the recorder is still recording, nothing was lost, and the
32	/// panel is hidden, so a note there would be read by nobody until the
33	/// landing, by which time it would be stale. A refused resume keeps the
34	/// recorder's sentence as `resumeProblem` and stays paused: the stream still
35	/// captures but no file is taking it, so what the person does next — try
36	/// again, or stop and land what was recorded — depends on the sentence, and
37	/// the landing's reveal (`revealIfNoted`, `+Landing.swift`) brings the
38	/// panel back with that sentence in its note when they stop. The sentence
39	/// is STATE and never text read back off the label (R2 review): the live
40	/// note is rebuilt from `[microphoneProblem, resumeProblem]` at every tick
41	/// (`syncMicrophoneNote`, over `liveNote` below), so a microphone
42	/// did-finish landing late cannot wipe it and a retried resume replaces it
43	/// rather than appending a second copy; and `landingNote` takes it as an
44	/// argument, so the landing's note carries it where the first shape — each
45	/// end replacing the label whole — dropped it, and the reveal showed
46	/// nothing. A resume that LANDS clears it: a sentence about a refusal the
47	/// person has since got past would bring the panel back with nothing true
48	/// to say.
49	///
50	/// A Stop while paused (`stopRecording`, `record(_:)`, File ▸ Stop
51	/// Recording) goes to `recorder.stop()` exactly as one while recording
52	/// does — the recorder's `.paused` arm takes the same finishing path with
53	/// the segment's output already closed — and the status item comes down at
54	/// `recordingEnded` as ever. The tick runs through `.paused` (`armTick`):
55	/// the meter poll is a no-op there, the recorder having silenced the bar at
56	/// the pause, and `elapsed` is frozen, so the footnote and the item hold
57	/// still on their own.
58	extension RecorderPanelController {
59	    // MARK: - Pause and resume
60	
61	    /// The status item's Pause Recording, and File ▸ Pause Recording's for
62	    /// the panel's own recording. `.recording` → `.paused`; any
63	    /// other phase beeps — the row was clicked in the moment between a Stop
64	    /// and the item coming down — and so does any throw, `.alreadyPaused`
65	    /// among them (the header).
66	    func pauseRecording() {
67	        guard phase == .recording else {
68	            NSSound.beep()
69	            return
70	        }
71	        do {
72	            try recorder.pause()
73	            phase = .paused
74	        } catch {
75	            NSSound.beep()
76	        }
77	    }
78	
79	    /// The status item's Resume Recording, and File ▸ Resume Recording's.
80	    /// `.paused` → `.recording`, with
81	    /// the refused-resume sentence cleared; any other phase beeps. A throw
82	    /// leaves the phase paused and keeps the recorder's sentence as
83	    /// `resumeProblem`, REPLACING an earlier one, redrawn into the note at
84	    /// once rather than at the tick's next turn (the header).
85	    func resumeRecording() {
86	        guard phase == .paused else {
87	            NSSound.beep()
88	            return
89	        }
90	        do {
91	            try recorder.resume()
92	            resumeProblem = nil
93	            phase = .recording
94	        } catch {
95	            resumeProblem = error.localizedDescription
96	            syncMicrophoneNote()
97	        }
98	    }
99	
100	    /// The live note's two parts, in order: the microphone's sentence, with
101	    /// the fact that the picture is still recording (a silent meter alone
102	    /// reads as a broken recording), then a refused resume's; empty with
103	    /// neither. Pure, so a probe can pin the composition without a recorder.
104	    static func liveNote(microphoneProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String?) -> String {
105	        var sentences: [String] = []
106	        if let microphoneProblem {
107	            sentences.append(
108	                "The microphone stopped: \(microphoneProblem) The picture is still recording.")
109	        }
110	        if let resumeProblem { sentences.append(resumeProblem) }
111	        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")
112	    }
113	
114	    // MARK: - The hidden recording's one door
115	
116	    /// The quit guard's call (`AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate`).
117	    /// While this panel is hidden for its recording `show()` can only beep,
118	    /// and a beep tells a person who paused and forgot nothing — so the
119	    /// status item's menu is opened instead, Pause or Resume and Stop put
120	    /// in front of them (`RecorderStatusItem.openMenu`); the beep is kept
121	    /// for the one case with no item to open. Any other recording — a
122	    /// tool's, which File ▸ Stop Recording ends — shows the panel as before.
123	    func revealControls() {
124	        guard hiddenForRecording else {
125	            show()
126	            return
127	        }
128	        if statusItem?.openMenu() != true { NSSound.beep() }
129	    }
130	
131	    // MARK: - The phases, drawn
132	
133	    /// Draws the phase: the button's title and enabled state, the controls
134	    /// locked while anything is in flight, the countdown numeral, the
135	    /// footnote, the camera preview (CAM-7), and the window refitted to
136	    /// whatever appeared or went.
137	    func syncPhase() {
138	        syncControlsEnabled()
139	        syncPauseButton()
140	        var countdown: String?
141	        switch phase {
142	        case .idle:
143	            recordButton.title = "Record"
144	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
145	        case .countdown(let remaining):
146	            recordButton.title = "Cancel"
147	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
148	            countdown = "\(remaining)"
149	        case .starting:
150	            recordButton.title = "Starting…"
151	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
152	        case .recording, .paused:
153	            recordButton.title = "Stop"
154	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
155	        case .stopping:
156	            recordButton.title = "Stopping…"
157	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
158	        case .landing:
159	            recordButton.title = "Adding…"
160	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
161	        }
162	        recordButton.invalidateIntrinsicContentSize()
163	        countdownLabel.stringValue = countdown ?? ""
164	        countdownLabel.isHidden = countdown == nil
165	        refreshStatusLabel()
166	        syncCameraPreview()
167	        fitWindowToContent()
168	    }
169	
170	    /// The footnote: the folder while idle, the coral dot and the elapsed
171	    /// time while recording, the pause glyph and the frozen time while
172	    /// paused — faint, because the dot's colour means "capturing" — and
173	    /// through `.stopping` whichever of those two it last showed, left
174	    /// UNTOUCHED (R2 review): the phase no longer says whether the Stop
175	    /// came from paused, `elapsed` is frozen at the stop call, and
176	    /// redrawing the arm as recording brought the coral dot back over a
177	    /// finish that captures nothing. The status item keeps its mark the
178	    /// same way (`RecorderStatusItem.freeze`, called by `stopRecording`).
179	    func refreshStatusLabel() {
180	        switch phase {
181	        case .recording:
182	            statusLabel.stringValue = "● " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
183	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.meterClip
184	        case .paused:
185	            statusLabel.stringValue =
186	                RecorderStatusItem.pauseGlyph + " " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
187	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
188	        case .stopping:
189	            break
190	        default:
191	            statusLabel.stringValue =
192	                "saved in " + (RecordingFiles.folder().path as NSString).abbreviatingWithTildeInPath
193	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
194	        }
195	    }
196	}

5	/// The half of screen recording a probe can call: values in, values out, no
6	/// framework object that needs a bundle (road map 3, R1a). What a recording
7	/// IS before it starts — the choice, where its files go and the two
8	/// ScreenCaptureKit configurations built from that choice (the two grants
9	/// it stands on are `RecordingGrant.swift`'s) — so that
10	/// `tools/proof/recording_probe.py` can read every field back from a bare
11	/// Mach-O that never starts a stream.
12	///
13	/// `ScreenRecorder.swift` (with `+Pause.swift`, `+Microphone.swift`,
14	/// `+Finishing.swift`, `+Delegates.swift` and `+Content.swift`) is the other
15	/// half: the class that owns the `SCStream`, one `SCRecordingOutput` per
16	/// SEGMENT (R2: a pause removes one and a resume adds the next) and, when a
17	/// microphone is chosen, the `AVCaptureSession` for the second file. The
18	/// result types a recording ends as — `StopReason`, `RecordingSegment`,
19	/// `RecordingResult`, `RecorderError` — are `RecordingResult.swift`, moved
20	/// off the foot of this file at the 400-line cap; they are still values a
21	/// probe can make.
22	///
23	/// Three R0 facts shape the configuration and are restated on the fields
24	/// they decide (`archive/roadmap-3.md`, "R0 — the answers"):
25	///
26	/// - **The microphone is a second file** (q2). `captureMicrophone` on the
27	///   stream writes ONE stereo track that is the SUM of system and microphone
28	///   sound, which is decision 5's bad case — so `make` never sets it, and
29	///   `RecordingChoice.microphone` names an `AVCaptureDevice` for
30	///   `ScreenRecorder`'s capture session instead.
31	/// - **`.best` does not scale by itself** (q4). `captureResolution = .best`
32	///   at the display's point size writes a point-sized file; pixels come only
33	///   when `width`/`height` are asked for in pixels, so `make` multiplies the
34	///   point size by the display's backing scale under `.best` itself.
35	/// - **Show Clicks needs BGRA** (q6a). `SCStream.h` says `showMouseClicks`
36	///   "currently applies when pixelFormat is set to BGRA" and a fresh
37	///   configuration reads `420v`, so `make` sets `REDACTED`
38	///   when the stream draws clicks and leaves the default alone otherwise —
39	///   measured, a recording output over a BGRA stream starts and writes. The
40	///   stream draws the pointer and its click ring only In the picture
41	///   (road map creator-jobs CU3c, spec §11 CU-31): with Separate, `make`
42	///   sets neither and keeps `420v`, and Show Clicks lands the screen clips
43	///   with ripples instead (`RecordingLanding+Cursor.swift`).

47	/// What is recorded. `.picked` is the panel's picker result, whose filter
48	/// is carried beside the choice (`ScreenRecorder.start` takes the filter as
49	/// its own argument), so the source enum never holds a framework object.
50	/// `.voiceOver` is the microphone alone, no picture (spec §11 recording, #99):
51	/// `ScreenRecorder.startVoiceOver` records it and `start` refuses it.
52	/// `.camera` is a camera alone, the device in `RecordingChoice.camera` (spec
53	/// §11 CAM-3): `ScreenRecorder.startCamera` records it and `start` refuses it,
54	/// while `start` records a camera beside a display, window or picked source (CAM-9).
55	enum RecordingSource: Equatable {
56	    case display(CGDirectDisplayID)
57	    case window(CGWindowID)
58	    case picked
59	    case voiceOver
60	    case camera
61	}
62	
63	/// `nominal` records the display's POINT size, `best` its pixel size
64	/// (`RecordingConfiguration.make` does the multiply — R0 q4).
65	enum RecordingResolution: String, CaseIterable {
66	    case nominal
67	    case best
68	}

70	/// Where the recording lands when it stops. `.document` carries the target's
71	/// `recipeKey` rather than an `ObjectIdentifier`: an identifier of a closed
72	/// document is reused by the next one at the same address
73	/// (`RelinkSheetController.swift` says so), while a `recipeKey` is never
74	/// minted twice, so `RecordingLanding.resolve`'s miss → `.newProject`
75	/// fallback is exact.
76	enum RecordingDestination: Equatable {
77	    case newProject
78	    case document(recipeKey: Int)
79	}
80	
81	/// Which keys a screen recording writes into its cursor files (road map creator-jobs CU6,
82	/// spec §11 CU-60, CU-62): none, or each shortcut spelled and a time-only mark for every other
83	/// key-down, under Input Monitoring. An enum so a later mode needs no rename; `record_screen`'s
84	/// `keys` spells it.
85	enum RecordingKeys: String, CaseIterable {
86	    case off
87	    case shortcuts
88	}
89	
90	/// Where a screen recording's pointer goes (road map creator-jobs CU3c, spec §11 CU-31, CU-36):
91	/// `separate` — not in the movie, written to the cursor file for Frame Job to draw — or
92	/// `inPicture`, burned in by ScreenCaptureKit as before CU3c. `record_screen`'s `cursor` spells it.
93	enum RecordingCursor: String, CaseIterable {
94	    case separate
95	    case inPicture = "in_picture"
96	
97	    /// CU-36 (b), (c), amended at CU0d: a window or picked recording's default. The
98	    /// quiet-machine re-run of CU-S2's window rows settled their anchor as E1, so it is
99	    /// `.separate`, as a display's is.
100	    static let windowDefault: RecordingCursor = .separate
101	
102	    /// CU-36, amended at CU0d: `.separate` for a display, `windowDefault` (`.separate`) for a
103	    /// window or a picked source, and `.separate` for a voice-over or a camera alone, which have
104	    /// no pointer to draw.
105	    static func defaultFor(_ source: RecordingSource) -> RecordingCursor {
106	        switch source {
107	        case .display: return .separate
108	        case .window, .picked: return windowDefault
109	        case .voiceOver, .camera: return .separate
110	        }
111	    }
112	}
113	
114	/// Every control of the recorder panel and every argument of
115	/// `record_screen`, as one value. `microphone` is an
116	/// `AVCaptureDevice.uniqueID`, nil for off; `rate` is 30 or 60 (a camera
117	/// recording's is its format's, `CameraDevices.canvasRate`). `camera` is an
118	/// `AVCaptureDevice.uniqueID`, set with `source` `.camera`, or beside a
119	/// display, window or picked source (CAM-9), and `cameraFormat` its format
120	/// as `CameraDevices.spelled` writes it, nil for Best and set only with
121	/// `camera` (spec §11 CAM-6).
122	struct RecordingChoice: Equatable {
123	    var source: RecordingSource = .display(CGMainDisplayID())
124	    var includeFrameJobWindows: Bool = false
125	    var microphone: String? = nil
126	    var systemAudio: Bool = true
127	    var showClicks: Bool = false
128	    var rate: Int = 60
129	    var resolution: RecordingResolution = .nominal
130	    var destination: RecordingDestination = .newProject
131	    var folder: URL = RecordingFiles.folder()
132	    var camera: String? = nil
133	    var cameraFormat: String? = nil
134	    /// Enhance Voice on the voice's clips after the landing; only with a microphone (AU-68, AU-69).
135	    var enhanceMicrophone: Bool = false
136	    /// Record shortcuts (spec §11 CU-62): only with a display, window or picked source.
137	    var keys: RecordingKeys = .off
138	    /// The Cursor row (spec §11 CU-36): nil follows the source's default.
139	    var cursor: RecordingCursor? = nil
140	    /// The polish on landing (spec §11 CU-100…CU-102): Auto Zoom, Add Shortcut Overlays and
141	    /// Speed Up Typing over the landed screen clips, each its own undo step after the landing.
142	    var autoZoom: Bool = false
143	    var shortcutOverlays: Bool = false
144	    var speedUpTyping: Bool = false
145	    /// The camera beside the screen's layout and its cutout on landing (spec §11 CO-80…CO-82).
146	    var cameraLayout: RecordingCameraLayout = .cornerSquare
147	    var cameraCutout: Bool = false
148	
149	    /// The cursor this recording is made with: the choice, else the source's default.
150	    var effectiveCursor: RecordingCursor { cursor ?? .defaultFor(source) }
151	}

153	// MARK: - Where the files go
154	
155	/// Decision 2 (road map 3 §0): a recording is ORIGINAL footage and lives in
156	/// `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by date and time — never in the
157	/// package (an untitled document has none) and never in the temporary
158	/// directory (where a cache is regenerable and footage would be lost). The
159	/// folder is created on demand, and `-RCRecordingFolder` overrides it the
160	/// way `-RCFFmpegPath` overrides the binary (`FFmpegRewrap.locate`), so a
161	/// proof can record into `tools/proof/work/` and delete it.
162	enum RecordingFiles {
163	    /// The launch-argument override, read from `UserDefaults.standard` so it
164	    /// works from the argument domain (`-RCRecordingFolder ~/x` on the
165	    /// command line, or a pinned volatile domain in a probe).
166	    static let folderDefaultsKey = "RCRecordingFolder"
167	
168	    /// The default folder's name under `~/Movies`.
169	    static let folderName = "Frame Job Recordings"
170	
171	    /// The folder a recording goes into: the override, tilde-expanded, when
172	    /// one is set; `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` otherwise. Nothing is
173	    /// created here — `create(_:)` is called at the moment a recording has
174	    /// something to put in it, `AppSupport`'s rule.
175	    static func folder() -> URL {
176	        if let override = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: folderDefaultsKey),
177	            !override.isEmpty
178	        {
179	            return URL(
180	                fileURLWithPath: (override as NSString).expandingTildeInPath, isDirectory: true)
181	        }
182	        let movies =
183	            FileManager.default.urls(for: .moviesDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first
184	            ?? FileManager.default.homeDirectoryForCurrentUser.appendingPathComponent(
185	                "Movies", isDirectory: true)
186	        return movies.appendingPathComponent(folderName, isDirectory: true)
187	    }
188	
189	    /// `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22` — the Screenshot app's
190	    /// spelling, in the machine's own time zone. The formatter is pinned to
191	    /// `en_US_POSIX` so a locale with another digit set or a 12-hour clock
192	    /// cannot change the name's shape; the seconds make a name unique across
193	    /// the app's own recordings and `uniqueURL` handles the rest.
194	    static func stem(at date: Date) -> String {
195	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
196	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
197	        formatter.timeZone = .current
198	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Screen Recording' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
199	        return formatter.string(from: date)
200	    }
201	
202	    /// `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04` — a voice-over's file, `stem(at:)`'s
203	    /// spelling and pinning with its own lead word.
204	    static func voiceOverStem(at date: Date) -> String {
205	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
206	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
207	        formatter.timeZone = .current
208	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Voice-over' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
209	        return formatter.string(from: date)
210	    }
211	
212	    /// `<stem>.<ext>` in `folder`, or `<stem> (2).<ext>`, `<stem> (3).<ext>`…
213	    /// while a file of that name exists — the Finder's own collision rule.
214	    static func uniqueURL(in folder: URL, stem: String, ext: String) -> URL {
215	        let manager = FileManager.default
216	        var candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent(stem).appendingPathExtension(ext)
217	        var counter = 2
218	        while manager.fileExists(atPath: candidate.path) {
219	            candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent("\(stem) (\(counter))")
220	                .appendingPathExtension(ext)
221	            counter += 1
222	        }
223	        return candidate
224	    }
225	
226	    /// The microphone's own file, beside the movie: the movie's stem plus
227	    /// ` (Microphone)`, as `.m4a` (R0 q6b: `AVCaptureAudioFileOutput` writes
228	    /// one mono 48 kHz AAC track there), made unique the same way.
229	    static func microphoneURL(beside movie: URL) -> URL {
230	        let stem = movie.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent + " (Microphone)"
231	        return uniqueURL(in: movie.deletingLastPathComponent(), stem: stem, ext: "m4a")
232	    }
233	
234	    /// Makes the folder, intermediate directories included. A folder that
235	    /// already exists is not an error.
236	    static func create(_ folder: URL) throws {
237	        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(
238	            at: folder, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
239	    }
240	}
241	
242	// MARK: - The configurations
243	
244	/// The two ScreenCaptureKit configurations a choice becomes. PURE — every
245	/// field is set from the arguments and read back by the probe — which is
246	/// what lets the `excludesCurrentProcessAudio` mutant be caught at all: it
247	/// is invisible over MCP (nothing plays during a headless recording) and
248	/// this is the only row that sees it.
249	enum RecordingConfiguration {
250	    /// System audio is asked for at 48 kHz stereo, the rate the tap and
251	    /// `Loudness.swift` already assume of every file.
252	    static let sampleRate = 48_000
253	    static let channelCount = 2
254	
255	    /// `displayPointSize` and `scale` come from the caller, and the caller is
256	    /// `ScreenRecorder.start`, which reads them off the FILTER — its
257	    /// `contentRect` (points) and `pointPixelScale` — the one geometry
258	    /// source that also covers a picker-made filter (`SCDisplay`'s
259	    /// `width`/`height` are POINTS, R0 q4, and a display filter reports the
260	    /// display's point size and backing scale, a window filter the window's
261	    /// frame). The probe passes the numbers directly. `outputURL` is
262	    /// assigned before the output configuration is returned, and must stay
263	    /// so: reading `outputURL` off a fresh `SCRecordingOutputConfiguration`
264	    /// TRAPS (it imports non-optional and is nil underneath until assigned —
265	    /// the SDK scout's finding, exit 133).
266	    static func make(
267	        _ choice: RecordingChoice, displayPointSize: CGSize, scale: CGFloat, outputURL: URL
268	    ) -> (stream: SCStreamConfiguration, output: SCRecordingOutputConfiguration) {
269	        let stream = SCStreamConfiguration()
270	        // R0 q4: pixels are asked for, `.best` does not scale by itself.
271	        let factor: CGFloat = choice.resolution == .best ? max(scale, 1) : 1
272	        stream.width = Int((displayPointSize.width * factor).rounded())
273	        stream.height = Int((displayPointSize.height * factor).rounded())
274	        stream.captureResolution = choice.resolution == .best ? .best : .nominal
275	        stream.minimumFrameInterval = CMTime(value: 1, timescale: CMTimeScale(max(choice.rate, 1)))
276	        // CU-31: the pointer and its ring are the stream's only In the picture.
277	        let inPicture = choice.effectiveCursor == .inPicture
278	        stream.showsCursor = inPicture
279	        stream.showMouseClicks = choice.showClicks && inPicture
280	        // R0 q6a: the click circle draws only under BGRA; the default `420v`
281	        // is left alone when the stream draws no clicks, so an ordinary
282	        // recording's pixel path is byte for byte the spike's.
283	        if choice.showClicks && inPicture { stream.pixelFormat = REDACTED }
284	        stream.capturesAudio = choice.systemAudio
285	        stream.sampleRate = sampleRate
286	        stream.channelCount = channelCount
287	        // ALWAYS: the timeline can play while a recording runs and must not
288	        // be in it. `captureMicrophone` is deliberately never touched (R0
289	        // q2 — the microphone is a second file), so it keeps its default of
290	        // false, which the probe reads back on every row.
291	        stream.excludesCurrentProcessAudio = true
292	
293	        let output = SCRecordingOutputConfiguration()
294	        output.outputURL = outputURL
295	        output.outputFileType = .mov
296	        // R0 q2: `availableVideoCodecTypes` is `[avc1, hvc1]` here and the
297	        // default is `avc1`; HEVC halves the file where the encoder offers it.
298	        output.videoCodecType =
299	            output.availableVideoCodecTypes.contains(.hevc) ? .hevc : .h264
300	        return (stream, output)
301	    }
302	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the

  revision, spec §11 G-34).

  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS

  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what

  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.
  `write(name:bytes:)` is `write(name:source:)` for bytes as they are, and
  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.

  (spec §11 G-27..G-29): `graphics/history/<name>/<%06d sequence>-<revision>.js`,
  the last `historyLimit` (10) per module, and `history/renames.json`, at
  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on
  the queue before it stores its scan, keeps the bytes a module's new text
  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not
  make, and `start()` drops each module's current revision from its history.
  `history/` is created only inside an existing `graphics/` (G-14) with no
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` call, and `moveHistory` leaves no
  `history/<from>/` behind — which is what makes 'no file, something kept'

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**

  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves

  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,

  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.

  every app-side writer goes through `write(name:source:)` or it. While the
  folder is absent the store watches the PACKAGE directory, and the first
  observed appearance calls `folderDidAppear` →
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` once — without it the next save is

  module, font and asset file has its own source, up to `fileSourceLimit` (16
  a pass, modules first, then fonts, then assets, each in name order; spec §11

  "`<subject>` is not watched: open failed (`<strerror>`)", `errno` copied
  first (G-20 (b); `GraphicScan.warnings`, shown by the Source section and `get_graphic {}`,
  G-24 (b));
  every pass re-opens every source BY PATH and
  arms BEFORE it scans; events coalesce over 100 ms. The queue owns the diff
  and an outbox; main publishes in order through `drain()` (`scan`, the
  callback, `.graphicsDidChange` with sorted names — every module and
  `library: true` when the font/asset set moved; with NO names when the
  folder holds no module and only the library moved, which still posts, G5b).

  `uniqueModuleName(_:)`, the one free-name rule (`-copy`, `-copy-N`)
  Duplicate and Insert ▸ Graphic share, which takes a name as held when the
  scan OR the disk has it (`holdsModule(named:)`, #75); `write(name:source:)`
  and `importFile` land through `land(at:writing:)`, whose `.partial` is
  removed on any failure; and `removeScratchRoot()`, which removes an untitled
  root after `stop()` — from `packageDidMove(to:)` and `stopGraphicStore()`
  (G-19 (d)). It also holds the app's delete and rename, each inside
  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.

  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.

  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on

  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

5	/// File ▸ New Recording… (⌥⌘N) — the recorder's panel (road map 3, R1c).
6	/// One instance for the life of the process, `ExportQueueWindowController`'s
7	/// mould (`shared`, a private init, `isExcludedFromWindowsMenu`,
8	/// `isReleasedWhenClosed = false`), because a recording outlives documents
9	/// and the panel must exist with none open. The controls become one
10	/// `RecordingChoice`; Record hands it to `ScreenRecorder.shared`; the result
11	/// goes through `RecordingLanding` into a document or opens a new one. This
12	/// file is the window, its rows and its phases; `+Rows.swift` is what fills
13	/// the popups, and `+Choices.swift` turns them into a `RecordingChoice` and
14	/// back;
15	/// `+Recording.swift` is everything from Record pressed to the recording
16	/// running, `+Grants.swift` the three grants a press checks first and the
17	/// one place System Settings is opened for them, `+Landing.swift`
18	/// everything from the recording's end to the note that says where it
19	/// went, `+Picker.swift` the window picker, `+Pause.swift` the pause
20	/// and the resume, the hidden recording's one door and the phases drawn
21	/// (R2c), `+VoiceOver.swift` the Source row "Microphone Only" (#99),
22	/// `+Showing.swift` `show()`, the sync timer, `setNote` and the refit,
23	/// `+Camera.swift` the Source row "Camera", its popup, the Format popup and
24	/// the "Record the camera too" box (spec §11 CAM-5, CAM-6, CAM-11),
25	/// `+CameraPreview.swift` the camera's live preview in `CameraPreviewWell`
26	/// (CAM-7), `+Devices.swift` hot-plug: the device observers and the
27	/// popups rebuilt when a device comes or goes (CAM-8), `+Polish.swift` the
28	/// "When it lands:" boxes (road map creator-jobs CU10, spec §11 CU-102), and
29	/// `+CameraLanding.swift` the camera's Layout and cutout (CO8, spec §11 CO-82).
30	/// Fourteen files at the 400-line cap, and the crossing members are internal
31	/// for it, the tree's rule for a class split across files.
32	///
33	/// **It is an `NSPanel`, floating and NON-ACTIVATING**, and each of the four
34	/// window settings below is load-bearing. `.nonactivatingPanel` so Record,
35	/// and the countdown's Cancel, can be clicked with the application about to
36	/// be recorded still FRONTMOST — the panel is off screen once the recording
37	/// runs (below), so this is for the seconds before it, when activating
38	/// Frame Job would put its document windows over the target; `.floating` so
39	/// it stays above that thing; `hidesOnDeactivate = false`
40	/// because `NSPanel` defaults it TRUE (`PreviewWindowController` measured it)
41	/// and a recorder panel that vanished the moment the person switched to the
42	/// application they are about to record would be useless; and NO window
43	/// delegate — a delegate that answers nil for the undo manager is the trap
44	/// `PreviewWindowController` records, and here there is no document to
45	/// answer with. It persists nothing about its frame (the queue window's
46	/// posture: no autosave name, no defaults key for the harness to pin), and
47	/// centres itself once; a panel is picked up and put beside the recorded
48	/// window each time anyway. **Whatever it is refitted to stays on the
49	/// screen it is on** (`fitWindowToContent`, R1 review): the countdown
50	/// numeral grows the card 88 pt DOWNWARD — 130 with a note under it — from
51	/// a fixed top edge, and a panel parked at the bottom of a display, the
52	/// natural place for a recorder, used to put its Cancel button under the
53	/// Dock.
54	///
55	/// **Visibility during a recording** (decision 7, R2c): the panel orders
56	/// OUT at `recordingDidStart` for every source but Microphone Only and
57	/// Camera (below), and the status item is the
58	/// recording's whole chrome — Pause, Resume and Stop are its menu; File ▸
59	/// Stop Recording still stops. R1 kept a DISPLAY recording's panel up, its
60	/// filter excluding Frame Job (R0 q3), and hid only a PICKED window's; the
61	/// user asked for the dialog to go away whatever is recorded, and a panel
62	/// whose one live control was a Stop the menu bar also has earned nothing
63	/// on screen. It comes back after the landing ONLY when it was on screen
64	/// as the recording began (`showWhenLanded`, read at `recordingDidStart`)
65	/// AND the landing left a note (`revealIfNoted`, `+Landing.swift`): a stop
66	/// from the system's own indicator, a closed target, a microphone problem,
67	/// a refused resume, a failure. A clean recording lands and the panel
68	/// stays away, and a panel closed before the recording began stays closed
69	/// whatever the note; ⌥⌘N shows it again. `show()` BEEPS while
70	/// `hiddenForRecording` (R1 review) — the welcome window's button reaches
71	/// it — because a panel un-hidden into the recording would be in the file;
72	/// the quit guard goes through `revealControls()` instead (`+Pause.swift`).
73	/// **It takes key only from an active Frame Job** (spec §11, #137): shown from
74	/// the background it is ordered front without key, so Return stays with
75	/// the app in front. **A voice-over stays UP** (#99): nothing is filmed, so
76	/// the rows lock, the meter stays live, Record reads Stop with a Pause /
77	/// Resume button beside it; Close takes the panel away and the recording
78	/// carries on — the welcome button and the quit guard show the panel again,
79	/// and ⌥⌘N (File ▸ Stop Recording) and the status item stop it. **So does
80	/// a camera recording** (CAM-5), on the same terms: nothing on screen is
81	/// filmed.
82	///
83	/// Two limits of that chrome, accepted (R2 review). With the panel hidden
84	/// the status item is the ONLY Pause and Resume, and macOS drops a status
85	/// item that does not fit the menu bar — behind a notch, in a crowded bar
86	/// — so there Stop survives in the File menu and Pause and Resume do not.
87	/// And "●" and "❚❚" differ in width under `variableLength`, so the items to
88	/// the left of it shift by a few points at each pause and resume.
89	///
90	/// **Quit while recording, and the order AppKit asks in.**
91	/// `AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate` cancels a quit while
92	/// `ScreenRecorder.shared.isRecording` and calls `revealControls()` — the
93	/// status item's menu, opened, while this panel is hidden for its
94	/// recording; `show()` for any other (a tool's, which File ▸ Stop Recording
95	/// ends) — and it is a BACKSTOP: `NSDocumentController` reviews modified
96	/// documents FIRST, so the save sheet comes before the guard, and a target
97	/// document the review CLOSED lands as `.newProject` —
98	/// `RecordingLanding.resolve` looks the destination up by `recipeKey`,
99	/// never minted twice, so the miss is exact, and the landing's note says
100	/// the document was closed.
101	///
102	/// **Two Record Into rules.** The popup is built from `NSMenuItem`s carrying
103	/// each document's `recipeKey` in `representedObject` and is read from
104	/// `selectedItem`, never by index: `NSPopUpButton.addItem(withTitle:)`
105	/// REMOVES a same-titled row (phase 4's defect), and two untitled documents
106	/// read alike. And it follows the FRONT document until the person chooses a
107	/// row themselves (`chosenDestination`), re-synced by a one-second timer
108	/// while the panel is visible — rows compared before any rebuild, so a menu
109	/// the person has open is never rebuilt under the pointer — **and only while
110	/// the phase is idle** (`rebuildDestinations`, R1 review): from the press
111	/// of Record to the landing the rows are FROZEN at what the person saw when
112	/// they pressed it, whichever document comes to the front meanwhile, and
113	/// `landed()`'s own rebuild is what moves them again. The destination the
114	/// recording actually lands in was captured from the controls at the
115	/// countdown's end and cannot move either way; what the freeze buys is that
116	/// the row on screen and the destination in the choice agree.
117	///
118	/// Every choice persists under a `FrameJobRecording…` key (written on change,
119	/// read on show); the harness pins all eighteen on `FrameJobExportChoice`'s terms.
120	/// `.picked` is the one source that cannot persist — a filter is not a
121	/// value — so a reopened panel with a picked window keeps the row only while
122	/// the filter is still held; Microphone Only and Camera persist for the
123	/// session only (the camera itself is remembered, the row is not). "Record
124	/// the camera too" (CAM-11) is remembered across launches, and so is Record
125	/// shortcuts (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-62), off by default, and
126	/// Cursor (CU3c, spec §11 CU-36), whose `""` follows the source's default,
127	/// the three "When it lands:" boxes (CU10, spec §11 CU-102), on, on and off
128	/// when never set, and the camera's Layout and cutout (CO-82), Corner and off.

368	    /// A countdown must not go on in a panel nobody can see: closing cancels
369	    /// it, and a microphone or camera the countdown prepared is let go with it — said
370	    /// again here rather than left to `cancelCountdown`, because a panel
371	    /// closed during the microphone PROMPT (before any countdown) may also
372	    /// hold one, and an input left open past the panel is the leak the
373	    /// discard exists to close (R1 review). A close while `.starting` is a
374	    /// Stop (R2 review) — the attempt abandoned before `launch`, the
375	    /// recording stopped after it, `stopRecording`'s own two arms — because
376	    /// a start that ran on behind a closed panel would read `showWhenLanded`
377	    /// false and land every later note where nobody sees it. A RECORDING
378	    /// carries on — the status item and File ▸ Stop Recording can end it —
379	    /// and the sync timer stops until the next `show()`. `panelClosing` is
380	    /// set FIRST, so the phase change below steps the preview to off and
381	    /// never builds a capture (CAM-7 (5)), the device observers go (CAM-8 (1)),
382	    /// and the well is emptied last.
383	    @objc private func panelWillClose(_ note: Notification) {
384	        panelClosing = true
385	        switch phase {
386	        case .countdown: cancelCountdown()
387	        case .starting: stopRecording()
388	        default: break
389	        }
390	        recorder.discardPreparedMicrophone()
391	        recorder.discardPreparedCamera()
392	        stopObservingDevices()
393	        syncTimer?.invalidate()
394	        syncTimer = nil
395	        cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
396	    }
397	}

246	            wanted.flatMap { key in
247	                destinationPopup.itemArray.firstIndex {

5	/// The recorder panel's choice: how the controls become one
6	/// `RecordingChoice`, how that choice is written to and read back from
7	/// `UserDefaults`, and the size note beside it. A pure move out of
8	/// `RecorderPanelController+Rows.swift` under road map "creator-jobs"
9	/// CU0a's toll U3.
10	extension RecorderPanelController {
11	    // MARK: - The choice, persisted and restored
12	
13	    /// The controls as one value. `.picked` only while the picker's filter
14	    /// is held; a "Window…" row with no filter (the picker was cancelled and
15	    /// the row not reselected) falls back to the main display. `camera` is
16	    /// the Camera popup's id while a camera is wanted (Source Camera, or the
17	    /// box beside a screen source: CAM-11 (3)), and nil otherwise;
18	    /// `cameraFormat` the Format popup's spelling beside it, nil for Best.
19	    func currentChoice() -> RecordingChoice {
20	        var choice = RecordingChoice()
21	        if voiceOverSelected {
22	            choice.source = .voiceOver
23	        } else if cameraSelected {
24	            choice.source = .camera
25	        } else if sourcePopup.selectedItem?.tag == Self.windowTag, pickedFilter != nil {
26	            choice.source = .picked
27	        } else {
28	            choice.source = .display(selectedDisplayID)
29	        }
30	        if cameraWanted {
31	            choice.camera = selectedCameraID
32	            choice.cameraFormat = selectedCameraFormat
33	        }
34	        choice.includeFrameJobWindows = includeFrameJobCheckbox.state == .on
35	        choice.microphone = microphonePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String
36	        choice.enhanceMicrophone = enhanceMicrophoneCheckbox.state == .on && choice.microphone != nil
37	        choice.systemAudio = systemAudioSwitch.state == .on
38	        choice.showClicks = showClicksSwitch.state == .on
39	        // CU-62: shortcuts only with a screen source; off for Microphone Only and Camera.
40	        choice.keys =
41	            recordShortcutsCheckbox.state == .on && !voiceOverSelected && !cameraSelected
42	            ? .shortcuts : .off
43	        // CU-36: the person's pick, nil for the source's default; none without a screen source.
44	        choice.cursor = voiceOverSelected || cameraSelected ? nil : cursorChosen
45	        choice.rate = Self.rates.contains(ratePopup.selectedTag()) ? ratePopup.selectedTag() : 60
46	        choice.resolution =
47	            RecordingResolution(rawValue: sizePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String ?? "")
48	            ?? .nominal
49	        if let key = destinationPopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? NSNumber {
50	            choice.destination = .document(recipeKey: key.intValue)
51	        } else {
52	            choice.destination = .newProject
53	        }
54	        applyPolish(to: &choice)
55	        applyCameraLanding(to: &choice)
56	        return choice
57	    }
58	
59	    /// Writes every control but the destination (a `recipeKey` is minted per
60	    /// process) and a picked window (a filter is not a value). The display
61	    /// key is left alone while the Window row, Microphone Only or Camera (the
62	    /// two session-only rows) is selected. The camera key, and the format
63	    /// key beside it (`""` for Best), are written only while the Camera popup
64	    /// names one, so "None connected" forgets nothing. The box's key is written
65	    /// on every change (CAM-11 (2)).
66	    func persistChoices() {
67	        let defaults = UserDefaults.standard
68	        if sourcePopup.selectedItem?.tag != Self.windowTag, !voiceOverSelected, !cameraSelected {
69	            defaults.set(Int(selectedDisplayID), forKey: Self.displayKey)
70	        }
71	        defaults.set(
72	            microphonePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String ?? "",
73	            forKey: Self.microphoneKey)
74	        if let camera = selectedCameraID {
75	            defaults.set(camera, forKey: Self.cameraKey)
76	            defaults.set(selectedCameraFormat ?? "", forKey: Self.cameraFormatKey)
77	        }
78	        defaults.set(systemAudioSwitch.state == .on, forKey: Self.systemAudioKey)
79	        defaults.set(showClicksSwitch.state == .on, forKey: Self.showClicksKey)
80	        defaults.set(
81	            includeFrameJobCheckbox.state == .on, forKey: Self.includeFrameJobWindowsKey)
82	        defaults.set(cameraBesideCheckbox.state == .on, forKey: Self.cameraBesideKey)
83	        defaults.set(enhanceMicrophoneCheckbox.state == .on, forKey: Self.enhanceMicrophoneKey)
84	        defaults.set(recordShortcutsCheckbox.state == .on, forKey: Self.keysKey)
85	        // CU-36 (d): the pick, never the row shown; `""` follows the source.
86	        defaults.set(cursorChosen?.rawValue ?? "", forKey: Self.cursorKey)
87	        defaults.set(currentChoice().rate, forKey: Self.rateKey)
88	        defaults.set(currentChoice().resolution.rawValue, forKey: Self.sizeKey)
89	        persistPolish(defaults)
90	        persistCameraLanding(defaults)
91	    }
92	
93	    /// The stored choices, each falling back to `RecordingChoice`'s default
94	    /// for an absent or stale value: a display no longer attached is the
95	    /// main one, a microphone no longer connected is Off, a camera no longer
96	    /// connected is the default camera, system audio is ON
97	    /// when nothing is stored (`bool(forKey:)` of an absent key is false, so
98	    /// the absence is tested by name).
99	    func restoreChoices() {
100	        let defaults = UserDefaults.standard
101	        if pickedFilter == nil, !voiceOverSelected, !cameraSelected {
102	            let stored = defaults.integer(forKey: Self.displayKey)
103	            selectDisplay(stored > 0 ? CGDirectDisplayID(clamping: stored) : CGMainDisplayID())
104	        }
105	        let mic = defaults.string(forKey: Self.microphoneKey) ?? ""
106	        selectMicrophone(mic.isEmpty ? nil : mic)
107	        let camera = defaults.string(forKey: Self.cameraKey) ?? ""
108	        selectCamera(camera.isEmpty ? nil : camera)
109	        let systemAudio =
110	            defaults.object(forKey: Self.systemAudioKey) == nil
111	            ? RecordingChoice().systemAudio : defaults.bool(forKey: Self.systemAudioKey)
112	        systemAudioSwitch.state = systemAudio ? .on : .off
113	        showClicksSwitch.state = defaults.bool(forKey: Self.showClicksKey) ? .on : .off
114	        includeFrameJobCheckbox.state =
115	            defaults.bool(forKey: Self.includeFrameJobWindowsKey) ? .on : .off
116	        cameraBesideCheckbox.state = defaults.bool(forKey: Self.cameraBesideKey) ? .on : .off
117	        enhanceMicrophoneCheckbox.state =
118	            defaults.bool(forKey: Self.enhanceMicrophoneKey) ? .on : .off
119	        recordShortcutsCheckbox.state = defaults.bool(forKey: Self.keysKey) ? .on : .off
120	        cursorChosen = RecordingCursor(rawValue: defaults.string(forKey: Self.cursorKey) ?? "")
121	        let rate = defaults.integer(forKey: Self.rateKey)
122	        _ = ratePopup.selectItem(withTag: Self.rates.contains(rate) ? rate : RecordingChoice().rate)
123	        let size = defaults.string(forKey: Self.sizeKey) ?? ""
124	        let resolution = RecordingResolution(rawValue: size) ?? RecordingChoice().resolution
125	        sizePopup.selectItem(at: RecordingResolution.allCases.firstIndex(of: resolution) ?? 0)
126	        restorePolish(defaults)
127	        restoreCameraLanding(defaults)
128	    }
129	
130	    /// The Cursor popup shows the person's pick, else the screen source's
131	    /// default: Separate for every screen source (spec §11 CU-36, amended at
132	    /// CU0d). Left as it is for Microphone Only and Camera, whose row is
133	    /// greyed with its value kept.
134	    func syncCursorPopup() {
135	        guard !voiceOverSelected, !cameraSelected else { return }
136	        let shown = cursorChosen ?? .defaultFor(currentChoice().source)
137	        if let item = cursorPopup.itemArray.first(where: {
138	            $0.representedObject as? String == shown.rawValue
139	        }) {
140	            cursorPopup.select(item)
141	        }
142	    }
143	
144	    /// `1728×1117 points · 3456×2234 pixels` for the chosen display; a picked
145	    /// window records at its own size, which the panel cannot know; a
146	    /// voice-over has no picture; a camera records at its best format. The
147	    /// Cursor popup is synced FIRST, before the three early returns, so the
148	    /// Window row (no `selectedScreen`) follows its source too.
149	    func refreshSizeNote() {
150	        syncCursorPopup()
151	        if voiceOverSelected {
152	            sizeNote.stringValue = Self.voiceOverSizeNote
153	            return
154	        }
155	        if cameraSelected {
156	            sizeNote.stringValue = selectedCameraSizeNote
157	            return
158	        }
159	        guard let screen = selectedScreen else {
160	            sizeNote.stringValue = "the picked window's own size"
161	            return
162	        }
163	        let size = screen.frame.size
164	        let scale = screen.backingScaleFactor
165	        sizeNote.stringValue =
166	            "\(Int(size.width))×\(Int(size.height)) points · "
167	            + "\(Int((size.width * scale).rounded()))×\(Int((size.height * scale).rounded())) pixels"
168	    }
169	}

16	    /// otherwise un-hide it into the recording. Shown while idle, a prepared
17	    /// capture that failed (or a build that threw) is let go first, so the
18	    /// preview's sync tries again (spec §11 CAM-7 (5)). The device observers
19	    /// are added before that sync, which applies a change made while the
20	    /// panel was closed (CAM-8 (1)).
21	    func show() {
22	        guard !hiddenForRecording else {
23	            NSSound.beep()
24	            return
25	        }
26	        panelClosing = false
27	        if phase == .idle {
28	            rebuildSources()
29	            rebuildMicrophones()
30	            rebuildCameras()
31	            restoreChoices()
32	            if recorder.state == .idle, previewFailure != nil { recorder.discardPreparedCamera() }
33	        }

35	        refreshSizeNote()
36	        fitWindowToContent()
37	        floatAgain()

40	            window?.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)

42	            window?.orderFrontRegardless()

44	        armSyncTimer()
45	        observeDevices()
46	        syncCameraPreview()

49	    /// One second, while the panel is up: the Record Into rows follow the
50	    /// documents that open and close and the one in front — while idle,
51	    /// which `rebuildDestinations` itself decides — and the camera preview
52	    /// steps again (CAM-7 (5)).
53	    private func armSyncTimer() {
54	        guard syncTimer == nil else { return }
55	        syncTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
56	            guard let self else {
57	                timer.invalidate()
58	                return
59	            }
60	            guard self.window?.isVisible == true else { return }
61	            self.rebuildDestinations()
62	            self.syncCameraPreview()
63	        }
64	    }

66	    // `syncPhase()` and `refreshStatusLabel()` — the phases drawn — are
67	    // `+Pause.swift`'s since the R2 review, the base file's toll.
68	
69	    func setNote(_ text: String) {
70	        noteLabel.stringValue = text
71	        noteLabel.isHidden = text.isEmpty
72	        fitWindowToContent()
73	    }
74	
75	    /// The window takes the card's fitting size, keeping its TOP-LEFT where
76	    /// it was — `setContentSize` would keep the bottom-left and walk the
77	    /// title bar up the screen every time the note appeared — and then
78	    /// CONSTRAINED to its screen (`window.screen`, else the main one), so a
79	    /// panel whose bottom edge sits near the Dock is pushed up when the
80	    /// countdown grows it rather than growing under the Dock (R1 review;
81	    /// measured, the numeral adds 88 pt below the rows and a note 42 more).
82	    /// `setFrame` itself constrains nothing — a window can be put anywhere
83	    /// programmatically, on screen or off — which is why the call is
84	    /// explicit.
85	    func fitWindowToContent() {
86	        guard let window else { return }
87	        card.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
88	        let content = NSRect(origin: .zero, size: card.fittingSize)
89	        var frame = window.frameRect(forContentRect: content)
90	        let current = window.frame
91	        frame.origin = NSPoint(x: current.minX, y: current.maxY - frame.height)
92	        let screen = window.screen ?? NSScreen.main ?? NSScreen.screens.first
93	        frame = window.constrainFrameRect(frame, to: screen)
94	        window.setFrame(frame, display: window.isVisible)
95	    }
96	}
